hypothesis: Two’s-complement arithmetic identities and scalar re-materialization can alter 64-bit instruction selection before register allocation. No compiler policy changes.

experiments.name: delta_repacked
delta_repacked_right

conclusion: Both scalar delta re-packing variants measured 100% at 96 bytes. Chose delta_repacked_right, which retains delta-first source addition and re-forms the delta from unsigned high/low scalar words. Unlike the prior union/aggregate materialization, this avoids memory and does not introduce extra instructions. Arithmetic complement/reassociation variants regressed. No flags, pragmas, or compiler changes.
semantics: For unsigned 64-bit delta, (((u64)(u32)(delta >> 32)) << 32) | (u32)delta is identically delta. No new memory accesses, undefined shifts, signed overflow, or externally visible operations are introduced.
